en: The Sūtra of the Jewel Casket Without Letters, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Northern Wei dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was dwelling at Vulture Peak in the great city of Rājagṛha.
At that time in the mountains,

there was a multitude of immeasurable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of great bodhisattvas surrounding the Tathāgata; all were of great wisdom, skilled in expedient means (*upāya-kauśalya*), courageous and diligent,
and well able to penetrate the dharma-gate of wordlessness.
He is well able to purify what is possible and what is impossible;
he is covered by the net of liberation through shame and remorse, and has tamed his sense faculties;
with the tusks of loving-kindness and compassion, and the tusks of shame and remorse, he takes pity upon all sentient beings.
They have attained the great samādhi, taking wisdom as their foremost priority and revering the Mother of Wisdom;
they are like a jewel island, a vast treasury of great treasures;
and they thoroughly understand all phenomena that are wholesome and unwholesome.
Awakened to the events of the three periods of time, all things are accomplished;
possessing wordless eloquence, they skillfully penetrate the two kinds of emptiness and attain the supreme, wondrous stage;
having well studied the various truths, they thoroughly realize the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*).
Boundlessly courageous and vigorous, they are without any attachment;
they are fully able to penetrate the supreme dharmas of intrinsic nature;
and they are well able to contemplate the two types of dharma-gates: the real and the unreal.
Manifesting birth from the womb while forever transcending birth and death;
skillfully awakening to the secret, skillfully knowing all signs;
protecting all nations and attaining great renown.
They all further attain the supreme name of the Supreme Treasury;
they attain the Treasury of Wordlessness and sleep forever in peace and tranquility;
and all their actions and endeavors are entirely virtuous and joyful.
His name is universally renowned; he has transcended the triple world and is able to rescue the sentient beings dwelling therein.
He has perfectly awakened to True Suchness and universally manifests Samantabhadra.
They manifest their bodies everywhere, with all faculties pure;
they are skillfully able to awaken to and penetrate their own bodies and the bodies of others,
and all have attained the accomplishment of clear and sharp wisdom.
They were as follows:

the Bodhisattva Victorious Resonance, the Bodhisattva Dharma Resonance, the Bodhisattva Victorious in All Parts, the Bodhisattva Dharma Eye, the Bodhisattva Thousand Marks, the Bodhisattva Accumulation of Eloquence, the Bodhisattva Victorious Contemplation, the Bodhisattva Ground-Purifier, the Bodhisattva Limit of Ground-Purification, the Bodhisattva Deeply Penetrating the Sound of the Ground-Limit, the Bodhisattva Earth-Resonance, the Bodhisattva Endowed with Eloquence, the Bodhisattva Supreme Accumulation, the Bodhisattva Flower-Eye, the Bodhisattva Utpala-Eye, the Bodhisattva Topknot, and the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī Resonance.

Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas such as these were beyond calculation; they were all youths who had come from other worlds as numerous as the sands of inconceivable Ganges Rivers, and all of them resided in the position of crown prince, awaiting their inauguration as Dharma Kings.
The Bodhisattva Victorious Contemplation was surrounded by immeasurable Śakras and Brahmās;
the Bodhisattvas Samantabhadra, Gaganagañja, and others were surrounded by the four great kings of the quarters and immeasurable universal monarchs (cakravartin).
The Bodhisattvas Mahāsthāmaprāpta and Avalokiteśvara were surrounded by immeasurable hosts of Brahmās;
the Bodhisattva Amoghadarśin was surrounded by many immeasurable kings Vaiśravaṇa.
The Bodhisattva King of Constellations was surrounded by immeasurable constellations and other world-protectors.

Furthermore, there were the Bodhisattvas Dispeller of Doubt and Destroyer of All Obstructions, who manifested their own bodies as the body of a Tathāgata and were surrounded by immeasurable Buddhas; as well as Śāriputra, Mahāmaudgalyāyana, Mahākāśyapa, and all others, who were entirely great Arhats.
The Bodhisattva Satyaparīkṣa and the Bodhisattva Viśeṣacintin were surrounded by immeasurable celestial maidens.
The Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyarāja and the Bodhisattva Bhaiṣajyasamudgata were surrounded by immeasurable retinues.

All those suns and moons within all the worlds of the ten directions, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, who had harbored pride by relying on their own majestic power, all came toward the place where the Buddha was.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s dwelling, he withdrew to stand to one side before the Tathāgata; there he saw that his own body was devoid of radiance, appearing like a mass of ink set beside Jāmbūnada gold.
These suns and moons, abiding before the Tathāgata, do not manifest themselves in this same way.
They have no intention to abide, nor do they wish to speak; lacking majesty and power, they are unable to manifest.
Surrounded by immeasurable devas, including Nārāyaṇa and others;
surrounded by immeasurable nāgas, including the great dragon-kings Mahādeva, Takṣaka, and Anavatapta.
The Gandharva King Supriya was surrounded by an immeasurable billion hosts of gandharvas;
the Garuḍa King Atṛpta was likewise surrounded by seven hundred million hosts of garuḍas, and they both came to where the Buddha was.
At that time, in all the worlds throughout this trichiliocosm, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, all the bodhisattvas there each made their request to their respective Buddhas.
Having invited the Buddha, the fourfold assembly surrounded him and arrived at Sahā, bringing with them supramundane articles of offering; they came to the place where the Buddha was.
After those bodhisattvas had made their offerings to the Buddha, each sat down upon a lotus throne.
At that time, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Viśeṣacintin who came to where the Buddha was and addressed him, saying:
"World-Honored One!
If the World-Honored One would grant me permission, I would venture to ask the Tathāgata about the two characters [of his name]."
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Viśeṣacintin, saying:
“Listen to your question; ask whatever you wish.

It was not for the sake of a single sentient being that the Tathāgata attained enlightenment at this place; rather, it was for the sake of you all, the great elephants among men, that I appeared here.”
At that time, the Bodhisattva Victorious Reflection addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
What is the one dharma that is to be eliminated by a bodhisattva?"
"What is that one dharma which has been realized and awakened to by the Tathāgata?
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Viśeṣacintin, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
"Brahmā! You have already fully matured immeasurable roots of goodness; sustained by the empowerment of all Buddhas, you inquire about the meaning of this phrase.
Well-spoken son of noble family!"
"Listen now attentively and reflect upon it well; I shall speak for your sake.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Viśeṣacintin prostrated at the feet of the Tathāgata and received [the teaching] upon his head.
The Buddha said,
“Good son, there is one kind of dharma that a bodhisattva should extinguish, namely, the dharma of greed.”
"Good son! This is one dharma that should be eternally extinguished. Good son!"
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should extinguish, namely, the dharma of anger.
Good son! This is that one dharma which should be extinguished forever.
"Good son!
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should extinguish, namely, the dharma of delusion.
Good son!"
This is one dharma that should be eternally extinguished. Good son!
Furthermore, there is another dharma that a bodhisattva should extinguish, namely, the view of self (ātma-dṛṣṭi).
"Good son! This is one dharma that should be eternally extinguished. Good son!"
Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should extinguish, namely, indolence.
Good son! This is that one dharma which should be extinguished forever.
Good son! Furthermore, there is one dharma that a bodhisattva should extinguish, namely, sleep. Good son!
This is one dharma that should be eternally extinguished.
Son of good family!
Furthermore, there is another dharma that a bodhisattva should extinguish, namely, craving and attachment.
"Good son! This is one dharma that should be extinguished forever. Good son!"
Furthermore, a bodhisattva should eliminate one dharma, namely, ignorance.
Good son! This is that one dharma which should be eternally extinguished.
At that time, the Brahmā Viśeṣacintin addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is this one dharma that all bodhisattvas protect and guard day and night?”
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Viśeṣacintin, saying: "Good son!
That which is called a bodhisattva does not exhort others to do what they themselves do not desire."
"Good son! If there are good sons or good daughters who protect and uphold this Dharma, those good sons and good daughters protect and uphold all the treasuries of the Tathāgata’s precepts."
Why is this? O son of good family!
Those who cherish their own lives do not kill; those who cherish their own wealth do not steal the property of others; those who cherish their own wives do not violate the wives of others.
"Good son! These sentient beings give rise to such a thought, saying: 'I respectfully comply with the True Teaching of the Tathāgata.
That good son should always diligently protect this Dharma with a devoted mind."
For what reason? Good son!

If there are good sons or good daughters who seek the unsurpassed, truly correct, and equal enlightenment of great bodhi, those people all seek it for the sake of happiness; there is no one who seeks their own suffering, for in the world there are only those who seek to experience pleasant sensations.
For this reason, I have spoken these words.
You should know, O sons of good family: "Do not exhort others to do what you yourself do not desire.
Sons of good family!
"This is one dharma that a bodhisattva should constantly protect day and night. Good son!
As you have asked, what is this one dharma that has been realized and awakened to by the Tathāgata?"
"Good son! There is not a single dharma that the Tathāgata has awakened to. Good son!"
To have no awakening regarding phenomena is the awakening of the Tathāgata.
Son of good family!
All phenomena are unborn, yet the Tathāgata realizes awakening; all phenomena are unceasing, yet the Tathāgata realizes awakening.
"Furthermore, son of good family!
The Tathāgata has realized awakening to the fact that the nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is free from the two extremes.
The Tathāgata has realized awakening to the fact that all phenomena are unreal."

"Good son! The Tathāgata skillfully explains the causes and conditions of karma; the Tathāgata skillfully realizes the causes and conditions of karma. All phenomena are bound by causes and conditions, and the Tathāgata has awakened to them skillfully."
"Good son!
Those causes and conditions are like flashes of lightning; yet that which the Tathāgata awakens to is free from cause and free from condition.
The Tathāgata says that there is no karmic retribution, for once he has attained perfect enlightenment, he experiences it as such."
The vast and magnificent treasury of all dharmas is that which the Tathāgata has realized. Good son,
for what reason is it called the "Vast and Magnificent Treasury"?
"Good son!
From what do all worldly and world-transcending wisdoms arise?
When those wisdoms observe correctly through the contemplation of reality, the prajñāpāramitā becomes exceedingly profound; at that time, that dharma is given the name 'Treasury' (garbha)."
“Good son! I also teach that all dharmas are like illusions and like mirages; this is what the Buddha has awakened to.
That the nature and characteristics of all things are of one flavor—the dharma of liberation—this is what the Buddha has awakened to.”
All natures and characteristics are the single flavor of liberation; this is the vast and magnificent treasury of all dharmas.
"Good son! If there is a good man or a good woman, there is furthermore one dharma which is that which the Buddha has awakened to."
Good son! That is to say:

all dharmas neither go nor come; they have no cause and no condition; they are without arising and without cessation; they are without thought and without non-thought; they are without increase and without decrease.
"Good son!

If a dharma is ultimately such that its self-nature and dharma-nature are not a self-nature; if a dharma cannot be expressed by means of analogies, nor can it be expressed even by means of names—this is the one dharma realized by the Tathāgata."

When this Dharma-gate of the Radiant Adornment of the Jewel Casket Without Letters of King Vaideha was being taught, even those bodhisattvas who had attained the tenth stage, as numerous as atoms, whose eyes could not perceive it, and all such assemblies, attained the mind of *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Such sentient beings as these realized the fruit of arhatship.
Furthermore, a number of sentient beings exceeding this count were liberated from the sufferings of hell and reborn among the devas.
Immeasurable bodhisattvas manifested hundreds of thousands of millions of various samādhi gates.
How much more so would it be of no benefit to speak at length?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Rāhula, saying:
"Are you able to receive and uphold the meaning of this True Dharma as I have taught it?"

When these words were spoken, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, nine hundred million bodhisattvas from worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges rose from their seats and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

"We are all able to uphold this Dharma-gate so that, within this Sahā world, it may circulate without interruption for the sake of all sentient beings in future ages, knowing that such a bodhisattva is a vessel of wisdom."
At that time, the four Great Kings addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We, too, are able to receive and uphold the meaning of the Dharma taught by the Tathāgata, so as to fulfill whatever the Bodhisattvas seek, provided they are suitable vessels for this wisdom.”
At that time, the World-Honored One surveyed the entire assembly and spoke these words:
"Good sons! It was not by cultivating merely a small amount of roots of goodness that I attained perfect enlightenment."
If those sentient beings are able to hear this true Dharma, they too must have cultivated no small amount of roots of goodness.

If they can receive and uphold this Dharma-door of the King of Vast and Sublime Jeweled Caskets Without Letters, or if they are able to hear it, such persons shall have already paid me homage, and shall honor and praise me.
"Good son! Such good men and good women shall carry the burden of bodhi upon their two shoulders.
Those people will attain uninterrupted eloquence and achieve the excellent purity of all Buddha-worlds."
At the time of their death, they shall behold Amitābha Buddha in person, surrounded by a great assembly of śrāvakas and bodhisattvas, standing before them;
they shall likewise see my own body atop this King of Mountains, Gṛdhrakūṭa, and behold this host of bodhisattvas.
"Good son! Those good men and good women shall have obtained for themselves a great treasury of the Dharma that is inexhaustible;
they shall attain the knowledge of past lives and will not be reborn in the evil realms."
“Good son! I now proclaim this Dharma-gate, which has never before occurred in all the worlds and is difficult to believe. Good son!”

If those sons or daughters of good family should have committed even a grave offense of immediate retribution, by virtue of their being well able to read, recite, receive, and uphold this supreme Dharma-gate—whether they write it themselves or encourage others to write it, whether they read and recite it themselves or encourage others to read and recite it, or whether they maintain it themselves or encourage others to maintain it—[they shall be purified].
"Good son!
I say that such a person, who does not see the evil realms, shall receive the prediction of enlightenment from all Buddhas.

Those bodhisattvas will all attain the five eyes, be endowed with all faculties, be protected and remembered by all Buddhas, and be sustained by all bodhisattvas; they shall extinguish immeasurable afflictions, and their karmic obstructions will immediately become pure."
“Good son! This final discourse which I have spoken here has never been uttered by me since I attained the Way and realized perfect enlightenment.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the great Bodhisattvas such as Vimati-vinodana, the various devas including Śakra-rāja, the Four Great Kings, and all the world—including humans, devas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and gandharvas—having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced.
The Scripture of the Jewel Casket Without Letters (Amoghapāśa-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī)
